claim: TP2 COLLECTIVE WALL ROOT-CAUSED TO A DEVICE-MODEL INCONSISTENCY AND FIXED; SGLANG TP2 PASSES THE TOKEN GATE. Root cause (subagent forensics, every link measured live): the lane-generated 2-GPU topology advertised simd_count 1024 (= 256 compute units, a full MI350X) while gem5 simulates 4 CUs; the product rocminfo shim reports the advertised count; aiter's get_cu_num() parses it and selects a split-K CK GEMM whose 970-workgroup grid assumes near-full co-residency, with early 'fixup' workgroups polling per-block workspace flags that later 'publisher' workgroups write. Under in-order workgroup admission with only 16 resident slots the first cohort is all pollers, publishers are never admitted, and both ranks spin deterministically -- the dispatch-1618 freeze. Proof: GEM5-SPIN traces showed flag polls reading zero forever with the flag region byte-identical over 10s, and EXTERNALLY WRITING THE FLAGS completed the frozen dispatch in 2s (kernel mechanics healthy; only the writers were missing). The suspected NCCL/transport layer was exonerated: all collectives including a valid reduce_scatter pass in isolation (new tools/qwen35_nccl_rsprobe_capsule.py with a numeric oracle), and the prior RS-ONLY 'deterministic deadlock' was a pre-existing client-side capsule bug (reduce_scatter_tensor with input==output violates the 2:1 size rule and raises ValueError before reaching NCCL) -- recorded as a retraction of CP-0123's per-collective interpretation. FIX: run_engine_lane.sh now rewrites each GPU node's simd_count to GEMSIM_NUM_COMPUTE_UNITS x simd_per_cu (default 4x4=16, CPU node untouched) so the stack advertises exactly what is simulated; the gpu-2 topology files updated; plus an inert-by-flag gem5 spin-trace instrumentation (dispatch-start logger + scalar poll-watch) as a keeper diagnostic, and the corrected rsprobe capsule.
